candidates.review_note: All twelve RNA-seq libraries are DLK1 perturbation replicates of the H295R adrenocortical-carcinoma cell line. The patient survival analyses in the publication use other data and no direct patient-tumor cohort is deposited here.

The public release contains 85 ACC patients with RNA expression and complete OS, and all 85 are retained. Its clinical workbook has DFS for 74 patients, but it does not expose additional RNA-profiled patients that could enlarge the OS cohort.

The pinned release retains the 33 independent NCI ACC tumors and excludes all 79 TCGA columns plus three noncohort identifiers before analysis. All 33 NCI profiles map one-to-one to positive OS times and explicit vital status; the immutable bundle passed repository QC with 52,895 non-ambiguous gene symbols.

The whole-transcriptome profiles can be linked to exact individual EFS, but the RNA subset was deliberately assembled as nine patients with good clinical evolution and five with poor metastatic or recurrent evolution. This future-outcome-conditioned ascertainment is incompatible with ordinary cohort survival analysis.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / pACT pediatric ACC study

candidates.review_note: The mixed 365-sample FFPE cancer series contains only three adrenocortical-carcinoma tumors. It therefore fails the ten-patient minimum, and GEO does not publish individual time-to-event data for these cases.

The 58 FFPE adrenocortical carcinomas were measured with a custom NanoString panel and GEO classifies the study as expression profiling by array. This is neither direct bulk RNA-seq nor a whole-transcriptome assay with at least 10,000 symbols.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / custom NanoString ACC study

candidates.review_note: This companion release profiles the same 58 FFPE adrenocortical carcinomas with a custom NanoString panel. GEO classifies it as expression profiling by array, so it falls outside both the bulk RNA-seq and whole-transcriptome gene-coverage requirements.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / custom NanoString ACC study

candidates.review_note: The advanced or metastatic adrenocortical tumors were profiled on the Affymetrix PrimeView expression array rather than by bulk RNA-seq.
The 57 metastatic lesions from 42 adrenocortical-carcinoma patients were profiled on Affymetrix microarrays. Multiple lesions do not change that the assay fails the direct bulk RNA-seq requirement.

The public project contains paired FFPE and frozen transcriptomes from three ACC patients, alongside three aldosterone-producing and three cortisol-producing adenomas. Only three patients match TCGA-ACC, far below the ten-patient minimum, and no individual time-to-event endpoint is reported.

The ENSAT study reports individual-center clinical follow-up for 179 oncocytic, 28 myxoid, 10 sarcomatoid and 1,098 conventional adrenocortical carcinomas, but it is a clinical and histopathology cohort without a matched public whole-tumor RNA-seq matrix.
candidates.source: ESMO Open / ENSAT rare-histology ACC cohort

candidates.review_note: A direct GraphQL audit found eight disease-matched adrenocortical-carcinoma participants with RNA-seq file records: three in phs002430 and five in phs002431. Every matched RNA-seq file is controlled, no public exact individual time/status endpoint is exposed, and the subset is below ten patients. Broad phs002677 matches were excluded because that study repeats study-level diagnosis lists on participant rows.
The release contains treatment experiments in human bladder-cancer and murine colon-cancer cell lines. It does not contain direct patient bladder-tumor bulk RNA-seq or individual clinical follow-up.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / platinum immunomodulation cell-line study

candidates.review_note: The study profiles BCG-naive and recurrent non-muscle-invasive bladder cancers by single-cell RNA-seq. It is not a direct whole-tumor bulk RNA-seq cohort.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / BCG-recurrent NMIBC single-cell study

candidates.review_note: The release contains one direct FFPE muscle-invasive urothelial-tumor bulk RNA-seq profile per patient and the publication shows an aggregate OS curve by subtype. Neither GEO nor the article supplements publish individual OS time and event/censor status, so that curve cannot be reconstructed at patient level.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / UNC BASE47 classifier study

candidates.review_note: The series provides one direct bulk RNA-seq FPKM profile for each of 11 young-onset bladder tumors, but GEO exposes no individual survival or recurrence time/status. The prognostic analyses in the publication use external adult bladder-cancer cohorts rather than follow-up from these 11 patients.
All 52 treatment-naive MIBC tumors map one-to-one to complete positive OS time/status. The source RPKM matrix contains 34,372 non-empty symbols that are unique under case-insensitive comparison.

All 73 primary T1 bladder tumors in the discovery cohort have direct bulk RNA-seq and individual recurrence time/status after bacillus Calmette-Guerin treatment. Explicit GEO Sample_description values link the JMT1 library identifiers to the count-matrix columns; 165 symbols with ambiguous Ensembl mappings are excluded.

The source study enrolled metastatic urothelial-cancer patients treated with immune checkpoint blockade. TCGA-TRACE restricts eligibility to the 78 RNA-profiled patients whose primary tumor location is bladder, excludes 11 upper-tract primaries, and retains only BACI165_1 for the one patient sequenced twice. GEO supplies individual OS time/status but does not define the exact time origin.

candidates.endpoint: PFS to muscle-invasive (T2+) and/or metastatic progression
candidates.review_note: The release retains 462 of 476 direct urothelial-bladder-tumor RNA profiles with positive progression-free follow-up. Fourteen zero-time censored records are excluded deterministically. The pinned source matrix contains 43,204 gene rows; one truncated SRXN1 row and symbols with ambiguous Ensembl mappings are excluded, leaving 37,909 analyzable symbols.

The two direct bulk RNA-seq cohorts expose 45 and 94 NMIBC profiles and binary recurrence labels, but not individual recurrence-free time or censoring time. The article makes patient-level clinical data available only by request, so a valid time-to-event endpoint cannot be reconstructed from the public files.
The bladder-cancer experiment is a single-cell RNA-seq study rather than direct bulk tumor RNA-seq and falls outside the repository assay contract.

The series contains 100 primary upper-tract urothelial carcinomas plus 13 expansion specimens. Upper-tract disease is not the same primary-site cohort as TCGA-BLCA, and the public article supplements provide aggregate clinicopathological summaries rather than individual survival time/status linked to the RNA profiles.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / upper-tract urothelial carcinoma study

candidates.review_note: The trial releases direct bulk RNA-seq expression and deterministic specimen-to-patient annotations for 300 patients, but GEO and all ten public article supplements omit individual PFS/OS time and status. Published survival associations therefore cannot be reconstructed as patient-level endpoints.

The public CPM matrix contains one primary non-muscle-invasive bladder-tumor profile per patient, and GEO labels 15 non-relapse, nine recurrence and eight progression cases. Neither GEO nor the public article supplement supplies an individual recurrence/progression time or censoring time; the reported median follow-up is aggregate only.

The series releases a complete FPKM matrix for 87 non-muscle-invasive bladder tumors and the article analyzes time to progression. GEO supplies micropapillarity and sex only, while the official supplement contains aggregate cohort characteristics rather than individual progression or censoring times linked to the RNA profiles.

The 51-series total combines RNA-seq, ChIP-seq and Hi-C from bladder-cancer cell lines and five patient tumors. Only four patient tumors have an RNA-seq profile; the remaining patient material is Hi-C or ChIP-seq. The direct tumor RNA subset is therefore below the ten-patient minimum and has no individual time-to-event endpoint.

All 65 libraries are perturbation experiments in human bladder-cancer cell lines or mouse bladder organoids. The series contains no direct patient-tumor bulk RNA-seq profiles or linked clinical endpoint.

The 28 primary, post-treatment and recurrent tumor libraries map to 14 patients from a cohort expressly assembled after acquisition of BCG resistance and progression to muscle-invasive disease. Inclusion therefore depends on a future outcome, and the complete public supplement provides only grouped clinical characteristics rather than individual OS, CSS or DMFS time/status linked to the RNA identifiers.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / BCG-resistant bladder-cancer longitudinal cohort

candidates.review_note: The discovery profiles are urinary extracellular vesicles from 16 bladder-cancer patients and the validation profiles are plasma extracellular vesicles from seven patients. No direct bladder-tumor bulk RNA-seq specimen is present, so this liquid-biopsy assay cannot extend the TCGA-BLCA tumor repository.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / urinary extracellular-vesicle bladder-cancer study

candidates.review_note: The 21 longitudinal profiles come from peripheral-blood monocytes collected from six bladder-cancer patients before and during BCG treatment. They are neither direct bladder-tumor profiles nor a ten-patient cohort, and no individual time-to-event endpoint is released.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / longitudinal BCG monocyte study

candidates.review_note: GEO contains 91 early-stage bladder-tumor profiles and 95 adjacent-normal profiles with tissue, sex, stage and grade. The study evaluates sex-related differential expression rather than a survival or recurrence endpoint; neither GEO nor the open-access article publishes individual time and event/censor status.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / early-stage bladder-cancer sex-difference study

candidates.review_note: The direct stage-T1 bladder-tumor profiles are classified as durable or non-durable BCG responders. The public deposit does not provide individual recurrence duration, censoring duration or another exact time-to-event endpoint, so the response label cannot be converted into survival data.

GEO releases pretreatment and post-treatment bladder-carcinoma RNA profiles from the NEODURVARIB trial, and the publication reports radiographic and pathologic response. Public clinical tables expose response categories rather than individual OS, PFS, recurrence or censoring duration/status.

The release contains one whole-transcriptome profile for each of 49 primary non-muscle-invasive bladder tumors and labels four patients as progressing. Four events fall below the repository minimum of five; independently, GEO does not publish individual progression or censoring duration.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / primary NMIBC whole-transcriptome cohort

candidates.review_note: GEO releases RPKM for 48 muscle-invasive bladder tumors and 38 adjacent tissues, but sample records contain no exact survival or recurrence time/status. GEO also lists no associated publication from which an individual endpoint table could be recovered.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / basal and luminal MIBC transcriptome cohort

candidates.review_note: All 24 RNA-seq libraries are biological replicates of parental or CD44-manipulated J82 and RT-112 bladder-cancer cell lines. Clinical-outcome analyses in the article do not provide a direct patient-tumor cohort.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / CD44v6 bladder-cancer cell-line study

candidates.review_note: The eleven pretreatment bladder biopsies are labeled BCG responder or nonresponder according to status two years after therapy. This fixed-horizon binary response does not provide exact individual recurrence or survival time with event/censor status.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO and Europe PMC / NMIBC BCG-response study

candidates.review_note: Thirteen pretreatment MIBC biopsies map to a public table containing OS months, but neither that table nor the four supplementary workbooks identifies whether each duration ends in death or censoring. Exact OS event reconstruction is therefore impossible.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO and Europe PMC / neoadjuvant cisplatin MIBC study

candidates.review_note: All libraries are gene-knockdown or control experiments in an engineered UMUC3 bladder-cancer cell clone.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / TRIM28-TERT bladder-cancer cell study

candidates.review_note: Ten double-negative MIBC tumors have a 19,398-target transcriptome panel and deterministic sample identifiers. Survival was analyzed in a larger 110-patient IHC cohort, while GEO and the complete official supplement provide no exact individual OS or DFS time/status linked to the ten expression profiles.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO and Europe PMC / double-negative MIBC study

candidates.review_note: The profiles are GRHL3-overexpressing and mock single-cell clones from EJ28 and SCaBER bladder-cancer cell lines.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / GRHL3 bladder-cancer cell study

candidates.review_note: All profiles are ACAT1-knockdown or control replicates in UM-UC-3 and T24 bladder-cancer cells.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / ACAT1 bladder-cancer cell study

candidates.review_note: All libraries are FDPS, SQLE or YY1 knockdown and control experiments in T24 cells.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / mevalonate-pathway bladder-cancer cell study

candidates.review_note: Thirteen direct FFPE NMIBC or MIBC tumors have public whole-transcriptome counts. GEO and all six official supplementary files provide tissue and CD44/CD44v6 annotations or expression results but no individual survival, recurrence or progression duration with event/censor status.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO and Europe PMC / CD44v6 bladder-cancer study

candidates.review_note: Ten pretreatment stage-IV tumors have public TPM and RECIST response labels, but only seven partial responses and three progressive-disease categories are released. No individual time-to-progression, survival or censoring endpoint is available.

candidates.study_name: Metastatic Bladder Urothelial Carcinoma (IMvigor210 Phase II Trial, ESMO Open. 2024) - iAtlas Harmonized

candidates.review_note: The 29 RNA profiles are pools of circulating tumor cells or circulating-tumor-cell clusters from ten patients, not direct primary or metastatic tumor-tissue bulk RNA-seq. No reusable individual time-to-event endpoint is deposited.
The expression libraries are MCF7 breast-cancer cell-line perturbation and multi-omic experiments rather than direct patient tumors.
The release contains Smart-seq2 single-cell profiles from 18 breast tumors. It is not a direct whole-tumor bulk RNA-seq cohort.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / breast-tumor vasculature single-cell study

candidates.review_note: The RNA-seq experiments use breast-cancer cell lines, xenograft-derived models and engineered metastatic-niche systems. No direct patient-tumor survival cohort is deposited.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / breast-cancer liver-metastatic niche study

candidates.review_note: The series consists of mouse and human breast-cancer cell-line experiments used to study dissemination. It does not contain direct patient tumor bulk RNA-seq with follow-up.

A whole-transcriptome FPKM matrix is public for metastatic ER-positive/HER2-negative tumors, and the paper reports an overall-survival Cox analysis. However, Supplemental Table 12 contains aggregate demographics only; neither GEO nor the public supplements provide patient-level survival time and event/censor status linked to the expression identifiers.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / metastatic ER-positive breast-cancer cohort

candidates.review_note: The transcriptional profiles are breast- and ovarian-cancer cell-line perturbation experiments with EPZ015666, not direct patient tumors.
The metastatic breast-cancer biopsies were profiled by single-cell RNA-seq. The series therefore falls outside the direct whole-tumor bulk RNA-seq contract.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / metastatic HR-positive breast-cancer single-cell study

candidates.review_note: The release contains 4T1 and MDA-MB-231 breast-cancer model perturbations rather than direct patient-tumor bulk RNA-seq.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / IL13RA2 breast-cancer model study

candidates.review_note: The RNA-seq libraries are MCF10A-derived experimental cell models used to test CHD1 dependency, not a patient breast-tumor cohort.
The series profiles isogenic T47D breast-cancer cell lines carrying SF3B1 alterations. It contains no direct patient tumors or clinical endpoint.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / SF3B1 isogenic breast-cancer study

candidates.review_note: The 23 RNA-seq libraries are repeated protocol and input-amount measurements from at most six breast tumors: three matched fresh-frozen/FFPE tumors and three additional archived FFPE tumors. The number of unique patients is below ten and no individual survival endpoint is deposited.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / FF versus FFPE technical study

candidates.review_note: Laser-capture RNA-seq was performed on histologically normal epithelial, stromal and adipose compartments from 16 healthy women and seven women who developed breast cancer two to six years later. These are not direct breast-tumor profiles and the future-diagnosis grouping is not a patient-level survival endpoint.

The matrix includes 18 breast-derived brain-metastasis RNA profiles with documented repeated specimens from one patient. The study defines OS from brain-metastasis detection, but publishes only aggregate summaries and curves; no individual time/status table linked to the RNA identifiers is public.

The SuperSeries combines CRISPR-screen, mouse, cell-line and circulating-tumor-cell subseries. Its only direct human patient component is single-cell RNA-seq of circulating tumor cells in GSE144494; it contains no direct whole-tumor bulk RNA-seq cohort.

The release profiles 135 freshly isolated single circulating tumor cells or cell clusters from 45 women. It is single-cell blood-derived expression rather than direct bulk tumor RNA-seq, irrespective of the publication's aggregate clinical associations.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / metastatic breast-cancer CTC study

candidates.review_note: The paired breast-tissue biopsies came from 30 women explicitly selected to have no personal or familial breast-cancer history. The experiment measures weight-loss-associated changes in non-tumor breast tissue and cannot represent TCGA-BRCA survival.

Eleven breast tumors were repeatedly profiled across fresh-frozen/FFPE and library-preparation protocols, and a processed normalized gene-count matrix is public. The technical study provides no individual survival or recurrence time/status; raw patient reads are additionally controlled through dbGaP.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / breast RNA-seq protocol comparison

candidates.review_note: This SuperSeries does not contribute an independent clinical cohort: its patient-tumor RNA-seq component is the already reviewed GSE148623 subseries, while the remaining records are breast-cancer cell-line, array, mouse or perturbation experiments. The GSE148623 patient subset itself retains only ten unique patients with eight PFS events and two censored observations, below the censoring minimum.

The tissue subseries provides a direct bulk tumor count matrix from HR-positive/HER2-negative metastatic breast-cancer specimens, but its public sample annotations expose disease state, treatment group and batch rather than individual progression or survival time and event/censor status.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / metastatic breast-cancer CDK4/6 study

candidates.review_note: The FFPE tissue subseries provides a tumor expression matrix, but public GEO annotations contain disease state, study group and batch only. No individual PFS/OS duration and event/censor status can be linked deterministically to the 54 profiles.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / metastatic breast-cancer CDK4/6 study

candidates.review_note: This accession duplicates GSE184869: both contain the same 45 matched primary-breast and brain-metastasis pairs, and their 16,714-gene processed XLSX files are byte-identical (SHA-256 1519f2400cc0e2e82a18599d7c6711745d48aa0107941baff5c9314c64d70f95). The publication designates GSE184869 as the source accession.

The release provides exome-capture RNA-seq for 45 matched primary-breast and brain-metastasis pairs and a complete 16,714-gene matrix. GEO and the public article do not provide individual survival or progression time/status linked to the 45 patients.

The RNA-seq subseries contains 11 patient-tumor profiles plus 32 breast-cancer cell-line libraries. The patient subset has exact PFS, but pt15 is represented twice; after one-sample-per-patient selection only ten patients remain, with eight events and two censored observations. It fails the minimum of five censored patients.

The RNA subset was assembled explicitly as 59 progressing and 64 non-progressing ductal-carcinoma-in-situ cases. GEO publishes the future-outcome class but not an individual event/censoring time. Outcome-conditioned ascertainment and the missing time-to-event endpoint each violate the repository contract.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / progressing and non-progressing DCIS study

candidates.review_note: All 36 RNA-seq libraries are treatment and JNK-pathway perturbations of MCF7 or T47D breast-cancer cell lines. The series contains no direct patient-tumor transcriptomes or individual clinical endpoint.

The series releases count and CQN-normalized matrices for 39 HR-positive/HER2-negative metastatic breast-cancer tumors treated with palbociclib and letrozole. Public GEO metadata expose treatment only and provide no individual PFS/OS time and event status; no associated publication is listed.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / PROMISE metastatic breast-cancer study

candidates.review_note: The processed matrix contains 34 breast-tumor profiles and six adjacent-tissue profiles, but GEO exposes only tissue identity. No publication, individual survival time or event/censoring status is available.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / breast tumor-adjacent transcriptome study

candidates.review_note: The release retains one source-designated invasive breast tumor per patient with exact positive OS time and explicit vital status. It excludes 417 endpoint-incomplete invasive profiles, extra regions, in situ lesions and experimental controls. Source-declared GRCh38 Ensembl release 104 mapping leaves 39,322 unambiguous symbols.

One treatment-naive breast tumor biopsy per patient is retained. Seventy-two of 87 RNA profiles have exact RFS time/status; the other 15 are excluded for incomplete endpoint data. Pinned GRCh37 release 75 mapping leaves 40,505 analyzable symbols.

The release retains the 15 pretreatment metastatic TNBC biopsies and excludes four repeated on-treatment profiles before endpoint QC. PFS is measured from biopsy to progression or death. GEO repeats the characteristic key tissue with biopsy timing and organ values; the study specification preserves both source values and explicitly selects the first value for parsing.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / Case Comprehensive Cancer Center

candidates.review_note: Restricted to primary invasive ductal carcinoma or adenocarcinoma in women younger than 35; DCIS and ambiguous histologies are excluded. The exact RSEM denominator is not encoded by ICGC, so the supplied scale is interpreted only within cohort.
The historical release has only 4 censored OS observations; a replacement cohort is required under the current endpoint QC policy.

The prospective CPTAC breast cohort has 121 tumor RNA profiles and 96 positive-time OS records, but only two deaths. Its PFS field contains no recorded events, so neither endpoint reaches the five-event minimum.
candidates.source: NCI PDC pan-cancer data freeze / CPTAC

candidates.review_note: The retrospective series deliberately selected patients with locoregional recurrence or distant metastasis and matched non-recurrent controls with at least five years of follow-up. This future-outcome-conditioned case-control ascertainment is incompatible with ordinary cohort survival analysis, irrespective of whether an exact recurrence interval can be recovered.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / TBCRC post-mastectomy recurrence study

candidates.review_note: The direct bulk RNA-seq series contains one triple-negative breast-cancer profile per woman and public demographic and clinicopathological metadata. The article supplement reports only aggregate two-year survival counts and no individual OS time/status or sample-level endpoint table, so survival cannot be linked to the expression profiles.
The targeted RNA-seq matrix contains only 2,559 gene columns, below the repository minimum of 10,000 unique gene symbols.

Whole-transcriptome counts are public for 76 baseline and 32 post-treatment breast-cancer profiles, but GEO provides no individual event-free-survival time/status. The article supplement reports aggregate outcomes only, so the baseline RNA profiles cannot be paired to a valid public time-to-event endpoint.

The series includes direct FFPE tumor profiles from ten inflammatory and four non-inflammatory breast-cancer patients, but neither GEO nor the indexed article exposes individual survival or recurrence time/status. PBMC, plasma, healthy-tissue and healthy-donor profiles cannot substitute for a tumor endpoint cohort.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / inflammatory breast-cancer TGIRT-seq study

candidates.review_note: The series provides raw whole-transcriptome counts for 100 breast-cancer brain metastases, but GEO and all seven official Cancer Cell supplementary files expose only sample descriptors, aggregate clinical summaries or model-level results. No public table links the RNA profiles to exact individual time-to-event durations and event/censor indicators.

The series releases direct bulk RNA-seq from breast tumors and normal tissues with exact accession, age, race, receptor and stage fields. The complete CC BY supplementary archive provides aggregate cohort characteristics and differential-expression results, not individual survival duration and event/censor status linked to the 155 RNA profiles.

The 89 profiles are RNA-seq and ChIP-seq perturbation experiments in SUM149PT, SUM159PT and MCF7 breast-cancer cell lines. Patient survival is discussed using external cohorts, but this GEO series contains no direct patient-tumor transcriptomes.

The 405 direct breast-tumor RNA profiles form the classifier-training subseries. An explicit sample-order audit of the 3,814-sample GSE81540 superseries shows that individual overall-survival fields begin at sample 406, the first GSE96058 validation sample. Neither GSE81538 nor its public supplements provide individual time and event status for the 405 training tumors.

This superseries is exactly the union of the 405-sample GSE81538 classifier-training cohort and the GSE96058 validation cohort. Only the GSE96058 component has individual survival and it is already promoted with 3,273 endpoint-complete patients; the superseries adds no new analyzable participant.

The trial release contains 455 breast-cancer profiles, but expression was measured with the HTG EdgeSeq Oncology Biomarker Panel, which interrogates 2,560 genes. The raw workbook and GEO processing metadata confirm this targeted panel, so it cannot meet the 10,000-symbol whole-transcriptome requirement irrespective of endpoint availability.

The public processed matrices contain 166 primary and metastatic breast-tumor profiles, including paired specimens, but GEO exposes only tumor type and sample identifiers. The survival analysis reported in the article uses the separate METABRIC cohort; no individual time/event endpoint is released for GSE147322, while raw and fuller phenotype data remain under dbGaP accession phs001866.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / paired primary-metastatic breast-cancer cohort

candidates.review_note: The 19 libraries profile sorted CD8-positive cells from peripheral blood, tumor and normal breast tissue rather than unfractionated breast tumors. Survival associations in the publication rely on other cohorts, so these immune-cell profiles cannot serve as direct TCGA-BRCA bulk-tumor validation data.

The release contains paired biopsy and surgery tumor profiles from ten women in a short presurgical dietary intervention, plus one technical replicate. It was designed to measure transcriptional change before surgery and publishes no individual survival or recurrence duration with event/censor status.

The 17 direct tumor profiles are baseline and cycle-one biopsies from only nine inflammatory-breast-cancer patients. The independent baseline cohort is therefore below the ten-patient minimum, irrespective of endpoint availability.

The series contains 42 pretreatment and 31 post-treatment breast-tumor profiles from approximately 42 patients and exposes vital status in GEO. It does not expose an individual survival duration or a linked primary publication from which exact time and censoring can be recovered, so vital status alone is not a valid time-to-event endpoint.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / longitudinal breast-cancer treatment cohort

candidates.review_note: Pretreatment whole-transcriptome profiles are public for 265 HER2-positive breast-cancer participants in CALGB 40601, but individual clinical outcomes are not released with GEO. The publication places the required patient-level clinical data under controlled access through dbGaP accession phs001570 or investigator request.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / CALGB 40601 HER2-positive breast-cancer trial

candidates.review_note: The OSLO_R release provides 93 direct breast-tumor RNA-seq profiles. The complete public source-data archive was inspected: sampleinfo_OSLO_R_t contains sample name, lymphocyte score, ER status, PAM50 and clustering labels but no survival or recurrence duration/status. Survival scripts in the archive use METABRIC, TCGA or legacy cohorts rather than OSLO_R.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO and Nature Communications source data / OSLO_R breast-cancer cohort

candidates.review_note: The superseries contains breast-cancer cell-line RNA-seq and chromatin perturbation experiments. Prognostic analyses in the study use external patient cohorts; this accession does not deposit a direct patient-tumor bulk RNA-seq cohort with linked follow-up.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / MYC enhancer cell-model study

candidates.review_note: GEO provides paired tumor and normal bulk RNA-seq from 43 patients with deterministic pair labels, but neither the accession nor the official supplementary datasets expose an individual survival or metastasis time with event/censor status for those patients.

The longitudinal neoadjuvant trial release contains 287 biopsies from 129 patients. Its public clinical workbook reports HER2 heterogeneity, treatment arm, hormone-receptor status, pathologic complete response and residual-cancer burden, but no exact individual survival or recurrence time/status.

The public cohort contains 222 pretreatment breast-cancer biopsies with whole-transcriptome TPM, age, receptor status, grade, stage and pCR/RD response. GEO publishes no follow-up duration or censoring status, and the associated open article models neoadjuvant response rather than releasing individual survival data. The aggregate statement that one TNBC residual-disease class had poorer survival cannot be reconstructed as a time-to-event endpoint.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO and open-access Frontiers article / neoadjuvant-response cohort

candidates.review_note: GSE123286 is a breast-cancer cell-line SuperSeries combining CRISPR screening, ChIP-seq, RNA-seq and ATAC-seq. Its RNA-seq subseries GSE123285 profiles ARID1A wild-type or knockout MCF7 cells under fulvestrant, tamoxifen or JQ1 perturbations. Neither accession contains patient tumors or patient-level clinical follow-up.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / ARID1A breast-cancer cell-line SuperSeries

candidates.review_note: The SuperSeries combines ChIP-seq in T47D and MCF7 cells, ChIP-seq in MCF7 xenografts and a 24-library RNA-seq subseries of T47D and MCF7 cells under estrogen or progestin conditions. The good-outcome statement is biological context; no direct patient-tumor RNA-seq cohort is deposited.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / progesterone-receptor breast-cancer cell-model SuperSeries

candidates.review_note: The series provides 95 pretreatment primary-breast-cancer bulk profiles and 27 public residual-tumor profiles with rich treatment, pathology and residual-cancer-burden annotations. Neither GEO nor the open article publishes individual event-free or overall-survival duration and censoring status; the study endpoint is pathological response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / Derouane neoadjuvant breast-cancer cohort

candidates.review_note: The RNA-seq and ribosome-profiling libraries are hypoxia, knockdown and small-molecule perturbations in MCF7-SIX1 and MDA-MB-231 cell lines. Patient-outcome associations in the article use external datasets; no direct patient tumors are deposited.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / eIF3 hypoxia breast-cancer cell study

candidates.review_note: The study RNA-sequences purified circulating monocytes and tumor-associated macrophages from breast and endometrial cancer cases. It does not provide direct whole-tumor bulk RNA-seq, and the reported disease-specific-survival association is evaluated in external tumor cohorts.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / breast and endometrial monocyte-macrophage atlas

candidates.review_note: The multi-omic series measures RNA and chromatin changes after MLL3, BAP1 or UTX depletion and EZH2 inhibition in human cancer cell lines. It contains no patient-tumor expression cohort or linked clinical endpoint.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / Polycomb-COMPASS cancer-cell perturbation study

candidates.review_note: The NEO trial provides serial direct breast-tumor profiles across 12,635 Ampliseq genes and reports an outcome association for an on-treatment biomarker. GEO sample metadata, the processed matrix and all four open supplementary files omit individual survival duration and event/censor status, so the published Kaplan-Meier result cannot be reconstructed.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO and Europe PMC supplements / NEO neoadjuvant trial

candidates.review_note: The mixed 52-tumor release contains only three breast-cancer profiles. The disease-matched subset is below the ten-patient minimum and GEO provides no individual time-to-event endpoint.

candidates.endpoint: PFS during palbociclib plus endocrine therapy
candidates.review_note: The public TPM matrix contains 64 source-designated baseline tumor profiles from 64 unique patients. Supplementary Table S1b supplies exact PFS months and progressive-disease status for all 64. Eight rows belonging to four case-insensitively duplicated symbols are excluded, leaving 20,226 unique symbols.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO and Europe PMC / Palbo-Bio prospective cohort

candidates.review_note: This GEO release contains endocrine and chromatin perturbation experiments in breast-cancer cell models rather than a patient-level tumor survival cohort.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / lobular breast-cancer chromatin study

candidates.review_note: The study releases metastatic biopsies, circulating-tumor-cell and peripheral-blood profiles from 21 stage-IV patients, but GEO and the open article supplements do not provide exact individual survival duration and event/censor status.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / stage-IV breast-cancer CTC and metastasis cohort

The 12 metastatic colorectal tumor profiles lack a public patient-level primary-site field that can distinguish colon from rectal cancer, so they cannot be assigned deterministically to TCGA-COAD versus TCGA-READ. GEO also omits an individual survival/progression duration and event/censor status.

The series contains paired bulk RNA-seq from 33 colon tumors and 33 adjacent normal tissues. GEO publishes disease state only, and neither the deposited matrix nor the linked article provides individual survival or recurrence time/status for the tumor patients.

The 24 pre/post-treatment profiles are 10x single-cell RNA-seq libraries from peripheral-blood mononuclear cells, not direct bulk tumor RNA-seq. The series therefore fails both the assay and tumor-tissue requirements.

candidates.review_note: All 49 source profiles are pathologist-reviewed stage-II primary colon tumors with one FFPE whole-transcriptome RNA-seq profile per patient. candidates.review_note: All 348 treatment-naive primary colon tumors map one-to-one to clinical records. DSS is additionally available for 320 patients with 72 events, and PFS for 348 patients with 109 events.

Both advertised RNA profiles are pseudobulk matrices obtained by summing single-cell RNA-seq counts per sample. They are not direct bulk RNA-seq assays and therefore fall outside the repository policy.

The paired series provide direct bulk RNA-seq for 140 mucinous and 119 non-mucinous colorectal cancers with age, sex and stage. Public supplements contain differential-expression, pathway, mutation and recurrence-gene summaries but no individual recurrence time/status linked to the GEO samples.

The series deliberately selects extreme favorable and unfavorable stage III colorectal-cancer outcomes. GEO exposes only no recurrence within five years versus recurrence within three years, without exact individual event or censoring times. Outcome-conditioned sampling and the missing time-to-event endpoint each independently fail repository policy.

The MEDITREME publication releases patient-level primary site and OS/PFS for the 57-person trial, while GEO releases 34 tumor RNA profiles under laboratory biopsy identifiers. No public crosswalk links those identifiers to trial subject IDs, and demographic or response-field matching is not accepted as deterministic linkage. The series also mixes colon and rectal primaries.

The series contains 150 colon tumors and 50 matched normal tissues, but GEO does not publish individual survival time/status linked to the RNA profiles. Its processed workbook exposes a limited targeted expression table with clinicopathological fields rather than a reusable whole-transcriptome matrix plus endpoint.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / Korean colon-cancer NTRK1 study

candidates.review_note: GEO releases RNA-seq from 12 TABAsCO trial tumors and 21 TAS-102 monotherapy controls under generic patient labels, plus one additional profile, but no individual PFS/OS time and status. The multicenter trial provides one direct bulk FFPE tumor RNA profile and individual surgery-anchored RFS for each of 37 patients with esophageal or gastroesophageal-junction adenocarcinoma treated with adjuvant durvalumab. candidates.review_note: A complete log2 FPKM matrix is public for 51 esophageal adenocarcinoma biopsies, and the publication states that survival data were available for all 51. GEO and all eight official supplements omit individual survival time and event/censor status.

The open supplement provides exact OS and PFS records for 79 RNA-profiled oesophageal adenocarcinomas, but the complete transcriptomes are restricted in EGA. Public source files contain derived immune and molecular results rather than a reusable whole-transcriptome matrix.

The updated series includes eleven esophageal adenocarcinoma tumors among Barrett oesophagus samples. Raw sequence is public, but no individual follow-up time/status is released, and the sole processed table contains isoform-switch results rather than complete gene expression.

The PNAS Dataset S6 workbook links all 23 source-labelled ESCC tumor profiles to positive Days OS and explicit Alive/Dead status. candidates.review_note: The transcriptomic experiments use human glioma cell lines treated with regorafenib and candidate combinations. No direct patient glioblastoma tumors or follow-up are deposited.

The release contains eight grade-4 IDH-wildtype glioblastoma tumors and three perilesional normal samples. Only eight tumor patients are represented, below the ten-patient minimum.

Only adult primary tumors labelled GBM and WHO grade IV are retained. The independent sequencing batch passes the event and censoring thresholds without pooling or batch correction.

Fifty-eight of 60 source-designated adult grade-IV glioma tumors have positive complete OS; two NA endpoint records and four normal brains are excluded. Two independent builds produced the same release ID and identical derived data. Pinned GENCODE v19 mapping excludes 293 ambiguous symbols and leaves 55,468 genes. The historical cohort includes twelve IDH1 R132H tumors and is not presented as a modern WHO IDH-wildtype-only series.
The historical release has only 3 censored OS observations; a replacement cohort is required under the current endpoint QC policy.

The 66 RNA-seq profiles are patient-derived xenografts rather than direct patient-tumor specimens. The study description and molecular profile explicitly identify the analyzed material as brain-tumor PDXs.

The recurrent-GBM bulk cohort has individual OS for all 47 tumors, but only four censored observations. It therefore fails the repository minimum of five censored patients without pooling or changing the prespecified endpoint.

The series contains 19 baseline tumor biopsies plus repeated pre/post specimens and publishes an OS duration in months for each sample. It does not publish an event/censor indicator in GEO, the article or the public supplementary archive, so the durations cannot be interpreted as a valid time-to-event endpoint.

Bulk counts are public for paired primary and recurrent tumors from 14 patients, but GEO provides only grade, IDH1 genotype and primary/recurrent labels. No individual follow-up duration and event/censor indicator is published, and the cohort also mixes glioblastoma with IDH-mutant grade-3 glioma.

The recurrent-GBM trial publishes raw counts, VIPER profiles, treatment arm and responder labels for 57 tumors. Its official supplement reports arm-level median PFS and response definitions but no individual PFS or OS duration with event/censor status linked to each RNA profile.

The authors' public analysis repository provides exact OS and death status linked to all 40 primary/recurrent RNA pairs. Every patient is recorded as dead, however, leaving zero censored observations; the recurrence-selected cohort therefore fails the minimum of five censored patients.

GEO provides gene-level TPM for 264 pretreatment diagnostic bone-marrow RNA-seq samples, but only tissue and library metadata. The article explicitly makes clinical data available on reasonable request. Its public survival supplement contains 939 UK-NCRI/AMLSG patients with identifiers that do not match the GSE297413 RNA samples, so no public individual endpoint can be linked to this expression matrix.

The series exposes direct bulk RNA-seq from diagnostic AML specimens, but its public supplements contain mutation lists and aggregate clinical/outcome summaries rather than individual OS, EFS or DFS time/status. Controlled dbGaP data are not publicly redistributable, and the GEO Patid identifiers cannot be positionally inferred to match the publication's Patient identifiers.

The direct diagnostic APL RNA-seq cohort is large and the publication notes that survival data were available for 321 patients, but the public clinical tables expose covariates and endpoint status without individual survival durations. The original supplementary appendix explicitly reports that no external public APL RNA-seq cohort with survival was available; durations must not be reconstructed from aggregate Kaplan-Meier results.

The public RNA-seq matrix contains seven diagnostic and six unpaired relapse specimens. Consequently, neither disease timepoint supplies the required ten independent patients, and GEO publishes no individual time-to-event endpoint for these profiles.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / inv(16) AML relapse study

candidates.review_note: The release contains diagnosis-time adult AML bulk RNA-seq for 506 patients and public age, sex, race, ELN and iScore annotations. GEO, the complete article supplements, source-data workbook and public code omit individual OS time/status and a deterministic bridge to any clinical table; the article makes the remaining data available only by request.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / Alliance AML iScore cohort

candidates.review_note: Whole-transcriptome TPM is public for 136 diagnostic AML profiles, but GEO exposes tissue, genotype and pretreatment status only. The primary article states that individual clinical and mutation data are available on reasonable request, and no public supplement supplies patient-level survival time/status.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / Taiwanese CEBPA AML cohort

candidates.review_note: The series contains 13 pretreatment AML bone-marrow transcriptomes and exposes only a binary survival-less-than-one-year label. It does not provide an exact individual follow-up duration with event/censor status, so the binary prognostic category cannot be converted into a time-to-event endpoint.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / ancestry-focused NPM1-mutant AML subset

candidates.review_note: The 22 libraries are paired treated and untreated ex-vivo AML-blast profiles from 11 patients. GEO publishes no individual survival time/status, and the paired chemotherapy perturbation design is not a diagnosis-time survival cohort.

The series contains 148 secondary-AML CD34-positive bone-marrow profiles within a 357-patient MDS/sAML cohort and a whole-transcriptome matrix. The complete Europe PMC supplement was audited: Supplemental Table 1 links patient IDs to diagnosis, age, sex, progression and mutations, but publishes neither individual survival duration nor event/censor status. The sAML subset therefore cannot support a public time-to-event analysis.

The release provides FPKM profiles for 248 AML bone-marrow samples and 50 healthy donors, but GEO supplies disease and tissue labels only. No linked publication or public clinical table provides individual survival or progression duration with event/censor status.

The 64 bulk profiles are repeated leukemia-subpopulation and treatment measurements derived from xenografts representing only four AML patients. The independent patient count is below ten, the material is not a direct diagnosis-time patient cohort and no individual time-to-event endpoint is published.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / AML leukemia-stem-cell xenograft study

candidates.review_note: All twelve libraries are untreated or ATRA-treated MOLM14 cell-line replicates with inducible RIP140 knockdown. Patient survival results in the publication come from external cohorts; this GEO series contains no patient-derived AML expression cohort.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / RIP140 AML perturbation study

candidates.review_note: The release contains treatment-naive AML PBMC RNA-seq from 24 patients selected as 12 low and 12 high type-I-interferon-index cases from a 132-patient study cohort. GEO and the complete official supplement do not publish individual OS or RFS duration/status linked to samples S1-S24, so the reported cohort-level prognosis cannot be reconstructed.

The bulk RNA-seq release consists of paired diagnosis and relapse specimens from six pediatric AML patients. The independent patient count is below ten and no reusable individual time-to-event endpoint accompanies the series.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / pediatric AML diagnosis-relapse study

candidates.review_note: The release contains 32 baseline AML profiles and three healthy controls. Supplementary Table S1 reports baseline characteristics, best molecular response and treatment response, but no individual OS, EFS or censoring duration/status linked to the RNA profiles.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / onvansertib plus decitabine AML trial

candidates.review_note: Public raw counts and response covariates are available for 142 AML patients, but the released workbook contains no individual OS or EFS time/status. Analysis code refers to additional survival workbooks that are not tracked in the public repository, so the endpoint cannot be reconstructed from public artifacts.

The patient-derived component is single-cell profiling in five patients, while the bulk RNA-seq component profiles sorted engineered T cells after co-culture with K562 model cells. It is not direct AML patient-tumor bulk RNA-seq with clinical follow-up.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / engineered T-cell AML model study

candidates.review_note: The 71-patient untreated older de novo CN-AML RNA-seq validation cohort is analyzed for OS and DFS, but the GEO samples contain no individual time/status. A later Alliance publication states explicitly that patient data used in survival analysis are available only upon reasonable request while generated molecular data are deposited in GEO.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / CALGB CN-AML validation cohort

candidates.review_note: The multi-omic series is a mechanistic drug-perturbation experiment dominated by Kasumi-1 AML cells, with a small ex vivo patient-cell component. It is not an observational direct-patient bulk RNA-seq cohort and contains no individual clinical time-to-event records.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / KIT-LSD1 AML perturbation study

candidates.review_note: Human induced-AML clones and primary AML cells were engrafted in mice, subjected to competitive growth or chemotherapy experiments, FACS-isolated from murine marrow and then RNA-sequenced. candidates.review_note: The prospective AML study releases longitudinal bulk blood and marrow counts and reports first-line response for 44 newly diagnosed patients. candidates.source: NCBI GEO / ETH Zurich AML pharmacoscopy cohort

candidates.review_note: The series profiles six FACS-sorted peripheral immune populations from 13 COVID-19 patients. The ten hematologic-cancer cases are not resolved as AML versus other malignancies and the expression is immune-cell, not direct leukemia bulk tissue.

The series consists of compound-treated HL-60 and ML-2 leukemia cell lines.

The adult primary WHO grade II-III subset remains an independent sequencing-batch release. CGGA IDs match expression exactly; recurrent tumors, pediatric cases and incomplete or non-positive OS records are excluded. Analysis is enabled while matrix redistribution remains disabled.

The adult primary WHO grade II-III batch remains separate from mRNAseq_693. The two batches share no CGGA identifiers or exact full clinical fingerprints. Analysis is enabled while source-matrix redistribution remains disabled.

The 2019 GLASS study is an earlier longitudinal release superseded by the promoted 2022 GLASS dataset. The cBioPortal records share 219 of 222 patient identifiers and 438 of 444 sample identifiers; the three old-only patients cannot independently meet repository QC.

Selected-gene files are insufficient for the 10,000-symbol requirement, so gene identities cannot be reconstructed reproducibly.

candidates.review_note: The hepatocellular-carcinoma trial release contains CITE-seq profiles of peripheral-blood mononuclear cells. It does not provide direct whole-tumor bulk RNA-seq.
The 164 liver biopsies come from 106 patients with NAFLD who were hepatocellular-carcinoma-naive at sampling. They are non-tumor liver profiles rather than an HCC cohort.

The phase-Ib trial deposits 12 liver-tumor expression profiles, but GEO provides no individual OS, PFS or recurrence duration with event/censor status. Treatment and response information alone does not constitute a time-to-event endpoint.

The release consists of longitudinal PBMC single-cell/CITE-seq profiles plus single-cell libraries from 16 live- or CD45-sorted tumor/adjacent specimens. It does not provide direct whole-tumor bulk RNA-seq and therefore falls outside the assay contract.

Exact publication patient-region identifiers link 393 tumor libraries to 110 patients. Before endpoint evaluation, one region per patient is selected by greatest total raw-count library size with lexical sample ID as tie-breaker; 109 have positive TTR. The endpoint remains labelled TTR rather than RFS, and direct matrix download is disabled under the combined source-license boundary.

The eligible subset contains 52 source-coded G1-G3 HCC tumors with individual postoperative DFS. One high-grade dysplastic-nodule profile and one combined HCC-intrahepatic-cholangiocarcinoma tumor are excluded. Two source technical replicates are linked deterministically to their unsuffixed clinical IDs, and all case-insensitive ambiguous gene symbols are excluded.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / Seoul National University Hospital

candidates.review_note: The public article supplement links all 41 HCC clinical labels to GSE202069 tumor profiles. TRACE Explorer prespecifies the 17 patients marked as receiving anti-PD-1 and excludes untreated tumors and nontumor columns before endpoint analysis. OS has 9 events and 8 censored observations; PFS is independently available with 11 events and 6 censored observations. The 31,082 source gene symbols are case-insensitively unique.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO and Europe PMC / Li et al.

candidates.review_note: All 70 source-labelled primary HCC tumors link exactly through the authors' RNASeq_T identifiers to complete positive OS time/status. Clinical Patient IDs then map one-to-one to the commit-pinned tumor-only expression columns. All rows assigned to 78 case-insensitive duplicated symbols are excluded, retaining 33,994 unambiguous genes. The immutable bundle passed repository QC.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO and authors' GPL-3.0 analysis repository / Mongolian HCC

candidates.review_note: The 42 tumor RNA profiles resolve to 21 unique individuals and were deliberately assembled from recurrent and non-recurrent outcome groups. The public release does not provide a valid individual time-to-event and censoring endpoint, so the future-outcome-conditioned design cannot support ordinary cohort survival analysis.

All 161 RNA-profiled donors have a primary hepatocellular carcinoma (ICD-O 8170/3), but only six expose usable overall-survival time and status. Four events and two censored observations fail the patient, event and censoring policy.

The immutable DataHub matrix provides 239 HCC TPM profiles, and the Nature supplementary clinical table provides operation, recurrence and death dates for the 494-case parent cohort. However, living and recurrence-free patients have no last-contact date or elapsed follow-up time, so neither OS nor RFS can be censored without inventing a study cutoff. Event-only times are insufficient for survival analysis.
candidates.source: cBioPortal DataHub / Chinese Liver Cancer Atlas

candidates.review_note: The cohort has clinical follow-up, but expression was generated with a targeted AmpliSeq panel covering 169 WNT-related genes rather than whole-transcriptome bulk RNA-seq. It cannot meet the repository minimum of 10,000 unique gene symbols.

The multiregional series contains 38 pretreatment and 32 post-treatment HCC RNA profiles from only eight unique patients, so it cannot reach the ten-patient minimum regardless of endpoint availability.

The study provides whole-transcriptome bulk RNA-seq from 73 advanced-HCC patients, including 73 pretreatment profiles, but GEO exposes only age, sex, diagnosis and biopsy timing. The article supplements report PFS and response only as aggregate tables and curves, with no individual time/status table linked to CU24 sample identifiers.

The GEO release contains single-cell gene-expression and T-cell-receptor libraries from pooled peripheral-blood mononuclear cells, not direct bulk hepatocellular-carcinoma tissue. It therefore fails both the assay and tumor-tissue estimand requirements.

Seventy-eight direct HCC tumors have public whole-transcriptome profiles, but GEO releases only tissue, molecular subtype and disease state. The article reports OS/DFS analyses and describes Table S1 as an overall clinicopathologic summary; its data-availability statement releases transcriptomic profiles only. No public exact individual endpoint duration and event/censor status can be linked to the YSH identifiers.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / Yonsei liver-cancer spectrum cohort

candidates.review_note: GEO provides whole-transcriptome profiles for 68 hepatitis-B-related HCC tumors and 10 adjacent tissues, with AJHCC identifiers and molecular subtype but no individual endpoint fields. The CGV publication demonstrates OS/RFS analysis of an HCC compendium containing GSE113617, but the public CGV source repository omits the external server-side clinical data objects. A plot-capable private server state is not a reusable exact patient-level endpoint.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO and public CGV source audit / HBV-related HCC cohort

candidates.review_note: The release combines single-cell RNA-seq, T-cell-receptor sequencing and CITE-seq from hepatocellular-carcinoma immune compartments before and after PD-1 blockade. candidates.review_note: The paired release contains bulk RNA-seq for 65 HCC tumors and 65 adjacent tissues, but GEO exposes only tissue labels. candidates.source: NCBI GEO / paired HCC expression-validation cohort

candidates.review_note: The release contains 113 resected nonviral hepatocellular-carcinoma tumors and the article reports class-level three- and five-year survival. candidates.review_note: The release contains nine combined HCC-cholangiocarcinoma and three hepatocellular-carcinoma group replicates. The release contains paired tumor and adjacent-tissue profiles from 30 patients. Its complete public workbook links sample IDs to radiological and pathological features but contains no individual survival or recurrence duration and event/censor status; it also includes AAH, AIS and minimally invasive lesions alongside invasive LUAD.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / early-stage LUAD radiopathology cohort

candidates.review_note: The bulk transcriptomes were generated from flow-sorted surface-IgA-positive and surface-IgG-positive memory B cells isolated from lung adenocarcinomas, not from whole tumor specimens. The publication's survival association uses TCGA-LUAD rather than an endpoint linked to these immune-cell profiles.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / lung tumor-infiltrating B-cell study

candidates.review_note: Fourteen patient tumors span five pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma histologies, with three normal-lung controls. The rare mixed cohort cannot be mapped reproducibly to TCGA-LUAD, TCGA-LUSC or TCGA-SARC, and GEO also provides no individual time/event endpoint.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma cohort

candidates.review_note: All twelve whole-transcriptome libraries are vitamin-C perturbation experiments in human NSCLC cell lines. The retrospective patient component was evaluated only by immunohistochemistry and is not part of the GEO RNA-seq release.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / vitamin-C NSCLC biomarker study

candidates.review_note: Human and mouse libraries profile myeloid progenitors, monocytes and macrophages across marrow, blood and lung tumors, not direct whole-tumor bulk RNA linked to patient survival.

GEO publishes 62 direct lung-tumor count profiles but only stage labels. The paper's survival workflow requires two undeclared Vanderbilt clinical files that are absent from the public code repository. Range-level inspection of the 2.55-GB open Zenodo archive confirmed RNA counts, batch metadata and a 92-patient pathology table, but no individual survival time/status.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO, GitHub and Zenodo / Lung Predict NSCLC study

candidates.review_note: RNA-seq, methylome and chromatin profiles track in vitro differentiation of primary human alveolar epithelial cells. They are non-cancer lung cells, not patient lung-adenocarcinoma tumors with clinical follow-up.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / alveolar epithelial differentiation study

candidates.review_note: The RNA-seq libraries are treatment and control replicates of A549, HCT116 and normal HSAEC cells; no patient tumor was profiled.
All profiles are PC9 lung-adenocarcinoma cells exposed to vehicle or ISRIB with or without asparagine for 6 or 24 hours.
This nascent-RNA time course profiles two cultured cell lines after DRB treatment and washout, not patient tumors.
The series contains vehicle, osimertinib, vitamin-D and combination treatments of H1975 and osimertinib-resistant H1975-OR cells.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / vitamin-D and osimertinib-resistance study

candidates.review_note: All RNA-seq profiles are parental, control-RNAi, PKC-epsilon-RNAi or KRAS-RNAi H2009 cell cultures.
The SuperSeries contains TIAM1 knockdown RNA-seq and chromatin-immunoprecipitation libraries from the H441 cell line; the clinical survival association was not generated from these profiles.
The public FPKM matrix contains paired normal and tumor organoids from eight LUAD donors. The unique-patient count is below ten, and no individual time-to-event endpoint is deposited.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / paired LUAD organoid cohort

candidates.review_note: All libraries are treatment and resistance experiments in pancreatic, colorectal or lung cancer cell lines performed in biological triplicate.
The series is a duplicated time course of TSA-treated A549 cells; survival predictions described in the summary use external patient data.
All profiles are A549 cultures with LKB1 or empty-vector constructs, methionine restriction and carboplatin treatment.

Seventeen bulk profiles represent sorted immature myeloid cells, neutrophils and epithelial cells from tumor or adjacent lung across six adenocarcinoma patients. The cohort is below ten patients and supplies no individual time-to-event endpoint.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / sorted NSCLC myeloid-cell study

Several sample title and disease labels are also internally inconsistent, so a deterministic disease-restricted endpoint cohort cannot be curated.

candidates.review_note: The public processed workbook contains only an Ensembl expression matrix for 41 pretreatment tumors. GEO provides treatment and genotype annotations but no individual survival, progression or recurrence duration and event/censor indicator, and no public histology key supports a separate LUSC endpoint cohort.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / pretreatment advanced or recurrent NSCLC cohort

candidates.review_note: Supplementary Data 1 and 4 expose 108 one-to-one SCC patient identifiers with exact OS time/status and matched primary-tumor expression. The promoted release excludes 8,065 genes with any source NA without imputation and retains 11,494 complete unique symbols.
