candidates.review_note: The RNA-seq reads are controlled-access; no openly redistributable processed patient matrix with linked endpoints was identified.
The public sample metadata contains treatment and SMRP covariates but no individual overall-survival time/status.
The 40-patient series publishes bulk RNA-seq but no individual survival rows; the survival analyses use the controlled Bueno cohort.
The survival-linked mesothelioma cohort is an Affymetrix expression-array study.

The 78 multiregional profiles map deterministically to 26 mesothelioma patients, but GEO contains tissue labels only. The paper and supplements use TCGA for prognostic validation and do not release survival time/status for the multiregional cohort.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / npj Precision Oncology supplements

candidates.review_note: The series contains paired CA125-positive and CA125-negative sorted tumor-cell subpopulations from ten high-grade serous ovarian cancers, not unsorted whole-tumor bulk profiles. GEO also provides no individual time-to-event endpoint.

The 21 records are gene-expression, TCR and BCR single-cell or repertoire assays from only seven HGSOC patients. The release is not direct whole-tumor bulk RNA-seq and is below the ten-patient minimum.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / HGSOC chemo-immunotherapy single-cell study

candidates.review_note: The ovarian component consists of OVCAR3 and related cell-line perturbation experiments with EPZ015666. No direct patient tumors are present.
The RNA-seq libraries are HO8910, SKOV3 and THP-1 cell experiments testing KLK5 overexpression. They do not form a patient HGSOC cohort.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / KLK5 ovarian-cancer model study

candidates.review_note: The release contains matched single-cell tumor-biopsy profiles from eleven patients across several solid cancers, only a subset of whom have ovarian cancer. It is neither a direct bulk assay nor a ten-patient ovarian cohort.

The cohort contains adult-type granulosa-cell tumors, including matched primary and relapse specimens. This sex-cord stromal malignancy is biologically distinct from the high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma represented by TCGA-OV, and no valid TCGA cancer mapping is assigned.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / adult granulosa-cell tumor study

candidates.review_note: All 93 RNA-profiled donors have usable OS. Primary tumor is preferred deterministically, with recurrent or metastatic tumor used only when no eligible primary profile exists.

One primary HGSC tumor is available per patient. Four records without a complete PFS time/status pair are excluded; the exact day-zero definition is not further specified by GEO and remains visible in the release metadata.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / CHA Bundang Medical Center

candidates.review_note: The primary paper identifies these as 83 newly and prospectively collected treatment-naive HGSC tumors independent of the earlier CPTAC-TCGA series. The PDC freeze contains 82 tumor RNA profiles; 79 have positive OS time and explicit status. GENCODE v34 mapping leaves 60,513 unambiguous symbols.

One FFPE omental metastasis maps directly to each source patient. A death at zero months is excluded, leaving 129 positive-time OS records. Twenty-seven Excel-corrupted MARCH/SEPT labels are repaired explicitly, and all 406 rows belonging to 66 case-insensitive duplicated symbols are excluded rather than averaged.

All 85 RNA-profiled treatment-naive primary HGSC tumors have exact positive PFS time and recurrence status. Pathology review includes ovarian, fallopian-tube and primary-peritoneal origins within the shared pelvic HGSC spectrum, so the release is mapped to OV but is not presented as ovary-site-specific. Pinned GENCODE v18 mapping leaves 55,113 unambiguous symbols.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / multicenter STIC-associated HGSC study

candidates.review_note: The verified Code Ocean capsule releases the exact BSSurvivalData.csv used in the paper, with 139 one-to-one Brescia HGSOC records, 101 deaths and 38 censored observations. All BS identifiers map deterministically to the corresponding GEO R-number columns. The source matrix contains 28,175 unique symbols and empirically represents nonnegative tximport estimated counts despite its TPM filename; TRACE Explorer therefore applies library-size CPM followed by log2(CPM + 1).
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / Brescia HGSOC / verified Code Ocean capsule

candidates.review_note: The cBioPortal view exposes vital status but no individual follow-up time. The same prospective CPTAC parent cohort is now represented canonically by the promoted PDC pan-cancer release, which supplies exact OS_days and OS_event fields; this incomplete view is not promoted separately.

The study profiles 39 patients with matched primary and metastatic tumors and labels 23 short-term and 16 long-term survivors. GEO, the CC BY article supplements and the public analysis code omit exact individual survival time/status; the outcome-defined classes cannot be converted into a reusable endpoint.

GEO provides direct bulk RNA-seq counts and clinical stage, age and histotype for 96 primary tumors, but no individual survival time/status. The open supplement reports only aggregate survival-duration categories and does not expose a sample-level endpoint bridge.

This SuperSeries contains the already reviewed RNA-seq SubSeries GSE101108 plus SNP-array profiles. It provides no additional transcriptomic cohort or patient-level survival bridge; the RNA-seq component remains rejected because only aggregate survival-duration categories are public.

A pinned 2026 clinical workbook deterministically links all 53 independent primary MOCOG tumors to 17 deaths and 36 censored observations, and the raw HTSeq matrix maps 55,531 unambiguous symbols. Nevertheless, every retained case is explicitly labelled a greater-than-ten-year survivor. Treating follow-up from diagnosis without delayed entry would introduce outcome-conditioned ascertainment and immortal-time selection. The 75 AOCS profiles are also excluded because they overlap the promoted OV-AU cohort.

The open CC BY 4.0 workbook provides exact OS for all 23 primary HGSC tumors and maps them deterministically to the GEO profiles, but all 23 patients died and were selected as short-term survivors. The cohort therefore fails the minimum of five censored observations and is outcome-conditioned. The accompanying 153-sample matrix is not promoted because it combines these cases with the outcome-selected GSE211669 cohort and AOCS/ICGC patients already represented in OV-AU.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / Zwimpfer et al. short-survival extension

candidates.review_note: The public RNA-seq profiles map longitudinal PRE and POST biopsies to 31 enrolled patients, but GEO and the open article do not provide individual PFS or OS time/status. The article states that additional deidentified participant data are available only by request.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / phase II pembrolizumab-chemo trial

candidates.review_note: Eighteen baseline biopsies have response category and a rounded response-duration field, but no explicit PFS time/status pair or censoring semantics. The associated article makes patient-level data beyond the publication available only by request.

GEO provides direct RNA-seq and sample-level histotype, stage and age. The CC BY article and all eleven public supplementary workbooks were audited, but they expose only aggregate survival summaries and derived analyses, not individual OS or DSS time/status.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / Australian epithelial ovarian cancer cohort

candidates.review_note: The 42 RNA-seq profiles represent multiple tumor or ascites specimens from 23 patients. The public supplement includes clinicopathologic variables but no individual survival endpoint; the survival cohort cited by the article is GSE49997, an external ABI expression microarray that is outside the direct bulk RNA-seq policy.

The CC BY source-data workbook reports PFS for 31 and 24 baseline RNA-seq patients, respectively, but only one observation is censored. Clinical rows also omit the GEO patient identifiers, so no explicit sample-to-endpoint bridge is public; either condition independently prevents promotion.

Twenty-seven baseline tumor profiles have exact PFS values in the later GSE318308 source-data workbook, but every patient has progressed. The cohort therefore cannot meet the policy minimum of five censored observations.

The study provides paired pre- and post-chemotherapy RNA-seq for 24 HGSOC patients and labels recurrence as early or late. It does not provide exact recurrence time/status or censoring, so the outcome category cannot serve as a survival endpoint.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / paired neoadjuvant chemotherapy cohort

candidates.review_note: GEO provides TPM for 37 pretreatment tumors with deterministic EOC sample identifiers. The CC BY supplementary appendix reports aggregate PFS and OS rates only, and the trial's data-sharing statement places deidentified individual clinical data behind request and ethics approval.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / TRU-D phase II trial

candidates.review_note: The public TPM matrix represents 111 patients, but the CC BY article's clinical supplement reports sample name, age, grade and FIGO stage without individual OS or PFS time/status. The source states that additional individual clinical data require reviewed access.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma study

candidates.review_note: The study releases 183 multiregional and longitudinal bulk RNA-seq biopsies from 50 patients. Public article supplements provide aggregate clinical summaries but omit individual OS or progression time/status linked to the profiles, so a one-profile-per-patient survival cohort cannot be constructed.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / multiregional longitudinal HGSOC study

candidates.review_note: The SDRF publishes individual progression-free duration but no event/censor indicator. Independently, the processed expression file contains only 155 immune-panel genes, far below the 10,000-symbol whole-transcriptome minimum.

The longitudinal series contains baseline and post-guadecitabine ovarian-cancer RNA profiles, with 33 baseline patients used in expression-versus-PFS analyses. GEO and the complete official supplement publish differential and PFS-associated gene results, not the individual PFS duration and event/censor pair required to link those baseline profiles.

The longitudinal bulk RNA-seq series mixes eight cancer types across 25 trial participants. Only four ovarian-cancer patients have baseline profiles, and some also have on-treatment biopsies. The disease-matched baseline subset is below the ten-patient minimum.

The 88-patient HGSOC series is explicitly a retrospective case-control study assembled by chemotherapy response, with responders defined using progression-free survival of at least six months. Enrollment therefore depends on a future outcome, and GEO publishes the response class rather than a complete individual time-to-event endpoint.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / HGSOC chemotherapy-response case-control study

candidates.review_note: The 15 direct ovarian-tumor profiles are labelled only as overall survival below six months or at least six months. This thresholded outcome lacks exact individual duration and event/censor status, so it cannot support a valid time-to-event analysis.

The baseline solid-tumor subset can be linked to 44 complete OS records and 47 complete PFI records, satisfying patient, event and censoring thresholds. However, the public processed matrix contains only 1,029 matrisome-targeted genes, far below the 10,000-symbol whole-transcriptome requirement.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / ovarian-cancer matrisome longitudinal cohort

candidates.review_note: The 417 measurements are NanoString GeoMx spatial regions of interest from fallopian-tube, ovarian, omental and lymph-node specimens in high-grade serous ovarian cancer. Region-level digital spatial profiles are not independent direct whole-tumor patient bulk RNA-seq samples.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / high-grade serous ovarian-cancer spatial atlas

candidates.review_note: The RNA-seq subseries GSE126131 contains only nine FACS-sorted cancer-associated-fibroblast libraries and is below the ten-patient floor. The 34-sample companion GSE126132 is an Illumina HumanHT-12 microarray, not RNA-seq; the larger clinical supplement is not linked to a qualifying whole-tumor RNA-seq cohort.

The mixed release contains ten ovarian-cancer tumors plus one borderline ovarian tumor. Although the disease-matched cancer subset reaches ten profiles, GEO exposes no individual survival, recurrence or progression duration/status; selection was based on retroelement expression rather than clinical follow-up.

The HGSOC series performs TruSight Oncology 500 deep targeted sequencing for mutations and gene fusions. It is not a reusable whole-transcriptome bulk RNA-seq expression matrix and cannot meet the 10,000-gene contract.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / primary-recurrent HGSOC targeted-sequencing cohort

candidates.review_note: The 39 profiles are repeated laser-capture-microdissected regions from only 15 high-grade serous ovarian-cancer patients. The reported survival analysis uses an external compendium of approximately 1,700 tumors; no exact individual endpoint is released for these 15 patients.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / spatially sampled HGSOC cohort

candidates.review_note: Twenty-two deposited tumor RNA-seq libraries link directly by patient number to the public clinical supplement. One zero-month RFS record is excluded, leaving 21 patients with 15 recurrences and six censored observations. The same SRA runs are uniformly reconstructed through pinned recount3 GENCODE v26 files, leaving 54,238 non-ambiguous symbols.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO/SRA, recount3 and PMC / UT Southwestern HGSOC ADP-ribosylation cohort

candidates.review_note: The ovarian component consists of cisplatin-sensitive versus resistant A2780 and OVCAR3 cell-line contrasts. The direct patient specimens in the SuperSeries are lung, not ovarian, tissues.

Eleven patients have matched primary ovarian and peritoneal or omental metastasis RNA-seq. Supplementary Table S1 links age, race, site and histology to each pair but provides no individual OS or PFS duration and event/censor status; the article's PFS plots use the external KM Plotter compendium.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO and PMC / matched ovarian primary-metastasis cohort

candidates.review_note: All libraries are quinacrine-treated or control platinum-sensitive and platinum-resistant ovarian-cancer cell lines.
The public count matrix contains primary and omental-metastasis profiles from only five patients, below the ten-patient minimum.

The disease-matched component contains six high-grade serous ovarian cancers; the other five libraries are fallopian-tube epithelium. Only six cancer patients are available and no individual endpoint is deposited.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / HGSOC and fallopian-tube epithelium study

candidates.review_note: The profiles are CD44-high/EpCAM-high and CD44-high/EpCAM-low fractions of OV90, CAOV3 and SKOV6 cell lines.
Five patients have matched primary and metastatic ovarian-tumor count profiles, below the ten-patient minimum; no exact time-to-event endpoint is released.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / matched ovarian primary-metastasis cohort

candidates.review_note: RNA-seq profiles FACS-purified PD-1-positive and PD-1-negative NK subsets from only two HGSOC patients, plus three healthy donors. The cancer-patient count is below ten.
All profiles are control, daphnetin or combination-treatment experiments in A2780 and SKOV3 cells.
The twelve libraries are NR1H3 knockdown, overexpression and corresponding control ovarian-cancer cell cultures.
The experiment compares NR3C1 knockdown and empty-vector SKOV3 cultures grown in two-dimensional or spheroid conditions.
All profiles are vehicle, cisplatin, nelfinavir or combination-treated IGROV-1/CP cell cultures.
The series contains treatment time courses in A2780 and isogenic A2780cis cells, not patient tumors.

cancers.review_note: The repository provides separate advanced POG570, Australian ICGC, Korean CHA, multicenter STIC-associated pelvic HGSC, prospective CPTAC, Cedars-Sinai omental-metastasis and Brescia HGSOC cohorts; they are not pooled.

candidates.review_note: The profiles are single-organoid and organoid-subclone experiments derived from eight pancreatic-cancer patients, not direct tumor-tissue bulk RNA-seq; the patient count is also below ten.
The RNA-seq libraries are PANC-1 and 2138 pancreatic-cancer resistance models treated with MRTX1133 and BET inhibition. No direct patient tumors or clinical outcomes are deposited.

The samples are pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors profiled by single-nucleus RNA-seq, not pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma represented by TCGA-PAAD. The assay also falls outside the bulk RNA-seq contract.

The RNA-seq component profiles Mel270 uveal-melanoma cells and HUVEC exosomal RNA; related ATAC-seq uses CFPAC-1 pancreatic cells. No direct pancreatic patient tumor or survival endpoint is deposited.

Seventeen direct FFPE PDAC bulk RNA-seq profiles and a deterministic sample sheet are public. The sheet contains treatment and batch only, while the local institutional analyses do not release individual survival time/status; the reported survival association uses TCGA.
The pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma trial profiles pancreatic biopsies by single-cell RNA-seq. It does not provide a direct whole-tumor bulk RNA-seq matrix.

The RNA-seq libraries are flow-sorted CD4, CD8, CD19 and CD11b tumor-infiltrating immune-cell fractions rather than direct whole-tumor bulk profiles. GEO reports only coarse OS classes (>2 years, <2 years or NA), not individual time and censoring status.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 PDAC study

candidates.review_note: GEO provides exact individual survival for 25 pancreatic tumors, but every profile is a 10x single-cell RNA-seq matrix rather than direct bulk tumor RNA-seq. The otherwise adequate endpoint cannot override the assay exclusion.

The series profiles peripheral-blood and manufactured multiantigen-targeted T-cell products with single-cell gene-expression and immune-receptor assays. It contains no pancreatic-tumor bulk RNA profile linked to survival.
All 161 expression patients matched GDC CPTAC-3 infiltrating duct carcinoma, NOS (8500/3); 158 had usable OS.
Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors and pancreatoblastomas are excluded.
Only primary tumors explicitly annotated as pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma are retained; invasive IPMN, acinar, adenosquamous, anaplastic and other histologies are excluded.
candidates.source: ICGC 25K Release 28 / Australian Pancreatic Cancer Genome Initiative

candidates.review_note: The pinned Bailey/QCMG matrix contains 96 profiles, but only 70 are exact primary PDAC. Fifty-two of those identifiers already occur in the active 66-patient ICGC Release 28 PACA-AU cohort. TRACE retains only the 18 exact-PDAC, endpoint-complete identifiers absent from that release; the two datasets therefore contribute 84 unique patients with zero identifier overlap. They remain separate because the source quantifications differ and must not be meta-analyzed as independent studies.
Primary project-designated pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas are retained. Many profiles are epithelial-enriched by laser-capture microdissection and remain a distinct analysis context.
candidates.source: ICGC 25K Release 28 / Canadian Pancreatic Cancer Sequencing Initiative

candidates.review_note: Only resected primary pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas are retained; companion pancreatic cell-line profiles are excluded.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / University of Alabama at Birmingham

candidates.review_note: Only the 79 whole-transcriptome profiles are retained. The matched exome-capture profiles are excluded before endpoint and expression QC so each patient appears once and platforms are not mixed.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / Medical College of Wisconsin

candidates.review_note: Only 218 source-designated primary pancreatic tumors are eligible. Two patients with T and T2 profiles are represented by the lexically prioritized T specimen, yielding 216 unique patients. The endpoint comes from the article's CC BY 4.0 RNA specimen table pinned to an immutable Git commit; the source study's optional exclusion of deaths before 30 days is not applied.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / Oregon Health & Science University

candidates.review_note: Only QC-valid pretreatment laser-capture microdissected tumor-cell libraries are retained. Stromal, post-treatment, surgical and technical-repeat profiles are excluded, and S025T1R1 is excluded using the source code's explicit low-depth QC decision. This first-line NP137 plus mFOLFIRINOX cohort remains a treatment-specific analysis context.

All 48 released bulk RNA profiles link deterministically to the CC BY 4.0 Supplementary Data 2 disease-free-survival records. Six additional clinical cases without released RNA are excluded. Source keys such as Pt 10 and GEO titles such as RNA-Seq PT10_1 are normalized by a recorded linkage rule; 248 ambiguous symbols are excluded.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center

candidates.review_note: GEO provides a complete 44-sample bulk RNA-seq count matrix but labels the samples only Sample1 through Sample44. The official CC BY supplements describe the RNA-sequenced treatment subsets and publish aggregate clinical tables, not individual OS/RFS duration and event status or a patient crosswalk. The article makes additional deidentified clinical information available only at author discretion, so no public deterministic survival linkage can be constructed.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / UT Southwestern neoadjuvant PDAC cohort

candidates.review_note: The direct patient-tumor bulk RNA-seq profiles and individual OS records are linkable, but only three patients are censored. The cohort therefore fails the prespecified minimum of five censored observations.

The pancreatic-cancer series is dominated by post-treatment and repeated specimens and does not publish individual survival or progression time/status. It cannot provide a one-primary-sample-per-patient diagnosis-time endpoint cohort.

The article reports 118 pancreatic cancers and aggregate survival counts, but the individual clinical records required to link expression with OS are available only through Hartwig controlled-access procedures.
The pancreatic-cancer study uses targeted spatial GeoMx transcriptomics rather than direct whole-tumor bulk RNA-seq.

The study contains exome-capture RNA-seq and prognostic data for 150 PDAC patients, but individual genomic, expression and clinical files require dbGaP authorization and cannot be redistributed as a public repository release.
candidates.source: NCBI dbGaP / Seoul National University Hospital

candidates.review_note: The SDRF provides deterministic patient/run linkage, exact OS months and vital status for 90 direct PDAC tumors, which pass endpoint QC. BioStudies supplies only raw FASTQ plus metadata; the full processed gene matrix is not public in the original study, later source-data files contain figure-level values only, and the R2 normalized cohort is available on request. The public FASTQ release remains a future reproducible raw-processing candidate; 14 PDX profiles are excluded.

The study deliberately selected five patients who died within 4-9 months and five patients who remained recurrence-free beyond 39 months, with two tumor profiles per patient. Because enrollment is conditioned on extreme future outcomes, this case-control RNA-seq set cannot estimate ordinary survival even though the groups are clinically described.

The 21 primary PDAC samples were profiled by single-nucleus RNA-seq and selected according to subsequent liver- versus lung-metastatic recurrence. The series is not direct bulk tumor RNA-seq and also lacks a public individual time-to-event endpoint.

This QuantSeq subseries profiles EpCAM-positive and EpCAM-negative fractions from the same resected MSK PDAC study represented by promoted GSE124231. It does not add independent patients, and the repository already exposes the direct RNA-seq tumor cohort with individual DFS.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / MSK PDAC QuantSeq subseries

candidates.review_note: GSE79670 is the parent superseries of the 51-patient tumor RNA-seq cohort GSE79668 and the pancreatic-cancer cell-line subseries GSE79669. GSE79668 is already promoted, so the parent series adds no independent patient data.

The bulk profiles are whole-liver biopsies obtained during pancreatectomy to study the premetastatic niche, not pancreatic primary tumors. Even though patients were followed for metastatic outcome, liver-tissue expression is not a disease-matched external TCGA-PAAD tumor cohort.

Eleven profiles are cultured patient-derived PDAC organoids and only three are direct original tumors from the same organoid donors. The direct-tumor subset is below the patient minimum, so the organoid transcriptomes cannot substitute for a primary-tumor survival cohort.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / PDAC patient-derived organoid study

candidates.review_note: The study profiles 16 pancreatic adenocarcinomas and 12 non-tumor pancreas specimens from different patients. GEO and the complete official supplements provide race, sex, age and tumor stage but no individual survival or recurrence time/status; survival analyses in the article use an external pancreatic-cancer database.

The 19 pancreatic-tumor profiles were deliberately selected as short-term or long-term PDAC survivors. This future-outcome-conditioned design cannot estimate ordinary cohort survival, and GEO releases the survivor class rather than exact individual time and censoring status.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / short- versus long-term PDAC survivor study

candidates.review_note: All 175 resected PDAC tumor profiles link exactly by unique GEO title to complete positive survival time/status, with 118 events and 57 censored observations. The source matrix contains 20,080 non-empty case-insensitively unique symbols and is imported unchanged because its CPM-TMM values include negatives. The article calls the endpoint overall survival while GEO names the status field cancer_death; TRACE preserves this as source-defined OS and records that ambiguity.

The pinned 396-column count matrix and GEO characteristics link deterministically by source sample ID. Excluding the one GEO sample absent from the matrix, 14 records with incomplete OS and two non-positive times leaves 380 unique pretreatment primary-PDAC profiles with 305 events and 75 censored observations. Ensembl release 95 maps the 60,671 source rows to 56,752 unambiguous analyzable symbols. The source publishes both OS and PFS; this release prespecifies OS and records that GEO does not state its clinical time origin.

The original article's survival summary includes 28 Linehan patients with 7 events and 42 Yeh-FNA patients with 30 events, but publishes only aggregate follow-up, median OS, subtype counts and model results. GEO exposes no individual endpoint. A later open-access analysis claims 44 GSE131050 survival cases, yet its official clinical workbook omits every GSE131050 record. Exact duration/status therefore remains unavailable.

GSE281129 is a SuperSeries whose bulk tumor component is GSE205154, already promoted as a 216-patient PAAD release with 171 OS events and 58,375 genes. Its other subseries, GSE281005, contains T-cell-receptor beta sequencing rather than an independent bulk transcriptome cohort. The SuperSeries adds no new analyzable patients.

GSE124232 is the SuperSeries containing ATAC-seq, QuantSeq and duplicate RNA-seq measurements from the same 54 resected MSK pancreatic cancers. The direct tumor RNA-seq subseries GSE124231 is already promoted with 48 exact DFS-linked patients; the parent series and QuantSeq representation add no independent participants.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / MSK pancreatic-cancer chromatin-accessibility SuperSeries

candidates.review_note: The phase-I solid-tumor study sequences T-cell-receptor repertoires in tumor biopsies and PBMC subsets before and after anti-CD4 treatment. It is not gene-level bulk RNA expression, and the small gastrointestinal cohort is not deterministically separable into pancreatic versus gastric primary cancers.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / IT1208 phase-I TCR-seq study

candidates.review_note: The expression and chromatin libraries are TP63 perturbation experiments in pancreatic cancer cells and in vivo models, not direct patient tumors linked to clinical survival.

candidates.review_note: The public clinical file identifies samples as P1-P29, whereas the Salmon TPM matrix identifies columns as GR129T01, GR111T01 and 27 other GR labels. GEO repeats the ordered GR label list in every sample record, but neither the series, its parent GSE263523 nor the linked supplementary tables provide an explicit P-to-GR correspondence. Mapping the two files by position and reproducing the published cycling-signature workflow yields a log-rank p-value of 0.02878, consistent with the reported p=0.029, but the resulting group sizes differ from the published risk table and therefore do not prove the 29 individual links. The two repeated patient IDs also carry different follow-up intervals, while the source does not define whether the interval starts at diagnosis or specimen collection. Positional inference and an unspecified time origin do not satisfy deterministic patient-expression linkage. A non-outcome-based rank would otherwise retain 27 patients with 21 deaths and 6 censored observations.

The direct bulk RNA-seq count matrix contains 54 central chondrosarcomas, but the public supplementary material reports only aggregate follow-up counts (49 alive, 3 disease deaths and 2 other or unknown deaths). It does not provide individual time/status rows linked to the RNA profiles.

The 23 direct bulk RNA-seq profiles have tissue, grade and depth annotations. The publication supplements describe separate imaging and immunohistochemistry survival cohorts, but do not expose individual time-to-event records linked to these 23 RNA samples.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / UPS and myxofibrosarcoma study

candidates.review_note: The direct FFPE RNA-seq series provides age group, tissue and molecular annotations, while the linked publication supplements do not include individual survival time/status records for the 22 RNA profiles.

The 119-column RNA matrix uses KH aliases and a separate open SARCOMICS workbook contains patient-level OS and DFS for 116 records identified by numeric Patient_ID. Neither GEO, SRA filenames, article supplements nor the related Zenodo record publishes a KH-to-Patient_ID bridge. Expression and endpoint data therefore cannot be linked deterministically.

The 69 profiles derive from 34 retroperitoneal-sarcoma patients with repeated specimens. Individual survival metadata are restricted rather than released with GEO, so one profile per patient cannot be linked to a public time/status endpoint.

The publication explicitly states that outcome data were unavailable for the 3SEQ expression samples; its survival analysis uses a separate immunohistochemistry tissue microarray. The RNA profiles therefore cannot support patient-level survival analysis.

The finalized article and open analysis release contain 122 RNA-QC tumors plus diagnosis-relative biopsy, recurrence and last-record dates. A sample-anchored local-recurrence endpoint can be derived for 55 patients (16 events and 39 censored), but the article explicitly states that the patient-partnered cohort is enriched for survivors. Enrollment or delayed-entry dates are not released, so ordinary survival analysis would retain outcome-conditioned ascertainment and left-truncation bias.
The open French leiomyosarcoma project contains clinical and mutation objects but no exp_seq objects.

The public TPM matrix contains 64 longitudinal bulk RNA-seq profiles from 27 DDLPS or UPS patients, and official figure source data expose exact RFS and OS time/status under clinical identifiers Acc 1-31. GEO, BioSample, SRA aliases and original FASTQ filenames identify the profiles only as Sample_1 through Sample_64. No public file maps those sample labels to the clinical Acc identifiers. The 23 baseline RNA profiles therefore cannot be joined deterministically to endpoint rows, and neither source-table order nor clinicopathological matching is accepted as a substitute.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / NCT03307616 neoadjuvant ICB trial

candidates.review_note: The normalized whole-transcriptome matrix contains 112 direct patient sarcomas plus five cell lines. GEO exposes tumor type, metastatic presentation, location and TRIO-fusion status, while the article reports only aggregate follow-up and relapse counts for the 112 tumors. Neither GEO nor the official supplementary tables provide individual time-to-event and censoring rows linked to the RNA sample identifiers.

The 41 libraries are pre/post-treatment technical replicates from only eight SARC037 Ewing-sarcoma patients. Even before endpoint availability is considered, the unique patient count is below the prespecified minimum of ten.
All 27 libraries are control and perturbation replicates from the LS8817 dedifferentiated-liposarcoma cell line. The series contains no direct patient tumors or linked clinical outcomes.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / dedifferentiated liposarcoma cell-line study

candidates.review_note: All thirteen RNA-seq libraries are chemotherapy and senolytic perturbation replicates of the MO-LAS-B and ISO-HAS-B angiosarcoma cell lines. The study contains no direct patient tumor profiles or clinical endpoint.

The mixed 52-tumor release contains three leiomyosarcomas and one nonspecific soft-tissue sarcoma. The disease-matched subset is below the ten-patient minimum and has no individual time-to-event endpoint.
The tumor and cerebrospinal-fluid specimens were profiled by single-cell RNA-seq. They are not direct whole-tumor bulk RNA-seq samples.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / melanoma CNS-metastasis single-cell study

candidates.review_note: The release contains murine CD8 T-cell and human Jurkat-cell experiments, with no melanoma patient tumors. Its SKCM mapping was a disease-keyword false-positive.

Thirteen melanoma-derived brain-metastasis RNA profiles are public, but the study releases only aggregate patient characteristics and mean survival. No individual survival duration and event/censor status can be linked to the RNA identifiers.

Direct melanoma tumor bulk RNA-seq and sample identifiers are public, but the individual PFS and OS clinical dataset is available only through the AstraZeneca data-sharing process. The open files therefore cannot support a reusable patient-level survival release.
The frozen RNA matrix contains 121 linked patients. The one transcriptome labelled On-PD1 is excluded; Pre-PD1, Pre-Ipi and On-Ipi biopsies precede the anti-PD-1 survival origin.

All 18 source-labelled on-treatment biopsies are excluded; the release contains one pretreatment profile for each endpoint-complete patient. PFS is also available with 22 events and 51 censored observations.
The single source-labelled on-treatment biopsy and one pretreatment patient without usable OS time/status are excluded.

Only source-labelled primary acral melanomas are retained. The profile is named FPKM upstream, but its negative, approximately gene-standardized values are preserved without an additional transform and exposed with an explicit scale caveat. DFS is also available with 10 events and 5 censored observations.

All 56 source-labelled on-treatment biopsies are excluded, leaving one pretreatment profile for each endpoint-complete patient. The immutable release includes the DataHub repository-level ODbL statement as its checksummed license evidence.

The release is restricted to treatment-naive primary cutaneous melanomas and excludes nevi. Forty-four of 51 tumor profiles have positive individual OS time/status; seven tumors without a complete endpoint are excluded. Repeat-element rows and case-insensitive ambiguous gene mappings are not silently merged.

Only the 17 source-labelled cutaneous-skin melanoma profiles are retained from the 25-patient adoptive-cell-therapy cohort; mucosal and unknown primaries are excluded rather than assigned to TCGA-SKCM. Expression was measured before ACT, although prior BRAF-treatment timing varies for a subset and is retained as a cohort-context caveat.

The public author repository links one pretreatment tumor profile to exact OS time/status for each of 71 ORIEN Avatar patients. Two independent builds produced identical source and derived checksums. Exact symbols recognized by the gene service are retained, and all rows belonging to duplicated recognized symbols are excluded rather than aggregated, leaving 36,690 genes. The source does not publish primary-site subtype per identifier, so mapping metastatic melanoma to TCGA-SKCM remains an explicit cohort caveat.
candidates.source: Europe PMC and author GitHub / ORIEN metastatic-melanoma ICI cohort

candidates.review_note: The release retains the 21 patients treated with hu14.18-IL2 who have complete individual OS. Group A tumors were resected after the first treatment course and group B tumors before treatment; this mixed expression timing remains explicit in the cohort context. Case-insensitive ambiguous gene symbols are excluded rather than merged.

The source's 45 acral bulk tumor profiles are kept separate from its sun-exposed comparator cohort. Forty-three patients have complete individual OS from resection; XY-12 and ZS-2 lack both time and event. All 18,928 source protein-coding symbols are unique case-insensitively.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / Yale and Central South University

candidates.review_note: The source's 60 sun-exposed bulk tumor profiles are kept separate from its acral cohort. Fifty-eight patients have complete individual OS from resection; LOVY and WW165 lack both time and event. All 18,928 source protein-coding symbols are unique case-insensitively.
Only seven of the 21 RNA profiles are source-labelled pretreatment biopsies; the post-treatment profiles are not substituted as baseline measurements.
This is a harmonized representation of the same Liu et al. patient cohort already released as mel_dfci_2019 and is not counted twice.
This is the original representation of the Hugo et al. cohort released through the curated iAtlas profile; it is not counted as an independent cohort.

GEO provides whole-transcriptome abundance, counts and effective lengths for pretreatment tumors and labels 24 relapses versus 33 relapse-free cases. Neither GEO nor the public article supplement exposes individual recurrence-free-survival time and censoring, so the binary relapse label cannot be converted into a time-to-event endpoint.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / pretreatment anti-PD-1 melanoma cohort

candidates.review_note: The direct bulk RNA-seq profiles map to 77 patients, but the open sample bridge and article supplements expose treatment-response categories rather than individual OS or PFS time/status. Aggregate Kaplan-Meier results cannot be inverted into reusable patient-level endpoint records.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / advanced melanoma immunotherapy cohort

candidates.review_note: The RNA-seq profiles were generated from peripheral-blood CD8-positive T cells rather than direct melanoma tumor tissue. The assay therefore falls outside the patient-tumor bulk RNA-seq policy.

The 75 profiles are from intermediate- to high-risk cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma, not cutaneous melanoma. Automated keyword mapping to TCGA-SKCM is therefore a disease mismatch regardless of the reported poor-outcome associations.
candidates.source: NCBI GEO / cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma cohort
Europe PMC and author GitHub / PUCH anti-PD-1 cohort
candidates.review_note: The CC BY 4.0 article points to the authors' public reproducibility repository, where 55 pretreatment tumor columns link exactly to positive OS time/status. Five additional clinical records lack expression and are excluded, leaving 10 deaths and 45 censored observations. The 20,293 supplied gene labels are non-empty and case-insensitively unique. Because the GitHub repository has no separate license file, TRACE disables redistribution while preserving pinned URLs, file hashes and the article's license evidence.

Sixteen paired pre/post profiles from eight melanoma patients were measured with the targeted HTG EdgeSeq Precision Immuno-Oncology Panel rather than whole-transcriptome RNA-seq. The RNA subset is below ten patients and has no exact time-to-event endpoint.
